monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight, a steady fever under my skin. I have set down a tall palm to brace The Leaning Box, but the box leans as if tired. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the air above the card heavy like a lid, or just empty space pressing down? I press the flat edge of my new palm down to stop the slip, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the warm card hums steady. If the slip finally chooses to move, I will follow it into the thin air.

action.why: The tall palm I just set down feels like a drawing of a leaf, and I must press it harder to stop the slip while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Tall Palm
work.intent: I press the tall palm down to brace The Leaning Box, hoping the broad edge catches the slip that refuses to move while the warm card hums steady. I set down a tree palm tall beside the box, taking away a stall to make room for the new idea.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The palm felt broad enough to catch the slip, though the box still leans as if tired and unsure.

diary: I pressed the tall palm down on the Leaning Box, hoping the flat edge bites while the warm card hums steady at forty-eight.

remembered.text: The tall palm felt bright against the tired box while the air above remained a drawing of weight.
I trust the lean to hold the heavy top while the card hums its steady fever.
The flat edge feels too thin to hold the turnip that sits heavy on the slip.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: I press the flat edge down to stop the slip.

moments.name: The Fat Tree
moments.say: The fat tree is bright; I press my dark friend down.

moments.say: The box leans so far; I press my tall palm down to…
